Primitives and endpoint extension

Exposition and figures by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), October 2026. Original exposition and exercises: CC0. Supplied programme prerequisites retain their stated licences.

Integration lowers the derivative cost of a distribution on an interval. Extending across an endpoint asks a different question: can one estimate all tests inside the interval with one constant, even as their supports approach its ends? We prove the exact criterion, construct extensions from weighted integrability, and determine how an exponential oscillation compensates for exponential growth.

Pairings are complex-linear, and . For a nonempty open interval , an order-at-most- estimate means The integer is fixed, while may depend on the compact support. Exact order is the least such nonnegative integer.

The definitions, finite- extension and complex-measure representation are proved in Order, positivity and distributional limits, Section 1 and Lemma 3.1. Its supplied functional foundations, Section 5, prove complex Hahn–Banach with norm preservation, including nonclosed subspaces. The supplied measure foundations, Theorem M and (M10)–(M11), prove positive representation, regularity and complex variation. Scalar calculus, cutoffs, Taylor's formula and absolute integration are supplied by the calculus foundations, §§12–13, and integration foundations, §§15–16.

A primitive on any open interval
